parts.title: Sequence words
parts.text: Sequence words tell us the order of an algorithm: First, Next, Then, Last. Use them to put the mixed-up step-cards in the right order.

teacher_guide.footer_topic: 2. First, Next, Then, Last — Teacher Guide

parts.title: Goal
parts.text: Students use the sequence words First, Next, Then, Last to order the steps of two everyday algorithms. Naming the order with sequence language is part of planning and representing a sequential algorithm (C3.1) and prepares students to describe how order affects the result (C3.2).

parts.title: Ontario curriculum (Grade 1 — C3 Coding)
text: C3.1 — solve problems and create computational representations of mathematical situations by writing and executing code, including code that involves sequential events.
C3.2 — read and alter existing code, including code that involves sequential events, and describe how changes to the code affect the outcomes.

parts.title: Materials
parts.text: The printed worksheet and a pencil. Optional: four cards labelled First, Next, Then, Last to place beside the step-cards.

parts.title: Run it (about 20 min)
text: 1. I DO: read the order words. 'First we get the bread — you can't toast with no bread.' Place First on card B.
2. WE DO: Exercise 1 — label the toast cards First B, Next D, Then A, Last C. Exercise 2 — write B, D, A, C.
3. YOU DO: Exercise 3 — get ready for recess: coat, zip, hat, outside (B, A, D, C).
4. Connect: 'Order words help you plan the steps before you do them — that is what coders do.'

parts.title: Answer key (modelled by the run-gate)
text: Ex 1 / Ex 2 — Make toast: First get the bread (B), Next put it in the toaster (D), Then push the lever down (A), Last take out the toast (C). Order: B, D, A, C.
Ex 3 — Get ready for recess: First put on your coat (B), Next zip it up (A), Then put on your hat (D), Last go outside (C). Order: B, A, D, C.
Why the order works: each step needs the one before — you zip AFTER the coat is on, and toast comes out AFTER it goes in. Swap two and the algorithm fails.

parts.title: Watch for & differentiate
text: Common slip: ordering by card letters instead of by the task — the letters are just names.
Simplify: do the toast task only, acting out each step as you place an order word.
Extend: ask students to make up a 4-step task and label it with First, Next, Then, Last.
Success indicator: the child labels each card with the right order word and writes B, D, A, C and B, A, D, C.
